carrier_name: Mutual of Omaha (United of Omaha Life Insurance Company)

must_contain: United of Omaha Life Insurance Company

extraction_notes:
Mutual of Omaha group proposals are multi-product documents (each product gets its own section with a header like "VOLUNTARY TERM LIFE AND AD&D INSURANCE", starting fresh page, with an "Alternate:" number). Structure per product: ELIGIBILITY block (class definitions, min work hours), BENEFIT SUMMARY block (min/max/increment/guarantee issue amounts in a table, benefit reduction schedule by age), then PARTICIPATION AND COST SUMMARY block with the actual rate table.

For "Voluntary Term Life and AD&D" specifically (this document had exactly this product with 2 sub-tables):
1. Voluntary Term Life rate table: single "Age Band" column of 15 rows (<25, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84, 85-89, 90-100), with rates per $1,000 - one column labeled "Employee & Spouse Rate per $1,000" (same rate applies to both classes) and one column "All Children Rate per $1,000" which is a SINGLE FLAT rate (only appears once, not age-banded - children get one flat rate regardless of age, printed only in the <25 row of the table but applies to all child coverage).
2. Voluntary AD&D rate table: separate small table with 3 flat (non-age-banded) rates per $1,000: Employee, Spouse, All Children - typically all equal to each other.
Employee benefit amounts: min/max/increment/GI in a 4-column table; separate benefit reduction schedule by age (e.g., age 60->65%, 70+->50%). Spouse and Child benefit amount tables follow similarly labeled "DEPENDENT SPOUSE BENEFIT AMOUNTS" and "DEPENDENT CHILD BENEFIT AMOUNTS".
Total count check: this document's Voluntary Term Life and AD&D product = 3 classes (Employee, Spouse, Child) for Life, each age-banded except Child (flat); plus 3 classes for AD&D, all flat rated equal amount to life. Note: other products in the doc (Basic Life/AD&D, STD, LTD, Dental, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Accident, Vision) exist elsewhere and should be IGNORED unless specifically requested - they use flat composite/tier rates (Employee, Employee+Spouse, Employee+Child(ren), Employee+Family) rather than age-banded life rates, and are laid out similarly with ELIGIBILITY/BENEFIT SUMMARY/PARTICIPATION AND COST SUMMARY sections per product, each starting on a new page with an "Alternate:" numeric code.
